raw_case_text: An antiretroviral therapy (ART)-naive woman was asymptomatic for tuberculosis (TB) at presentation and started on first-line ART (see Table 1 for more information). She rapidly deteriorated and presented again after 10 days with night sweats, a cough, and abdominal pain. She met the criteria for AlereLAM testing on this date, which revealed a strongly positive (4+) result. The patient was placed onto TB treatment and sputum was sent for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and mycobacterial culture, along with urine for mycobacterial culture.

subjective.chief_complaint: An ART-naive woman presented with night sweats, cough, and abdominal pain ten days after initiating first-line antiretroviral therapy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: An ART-naive woman with newly diagnosed HIV was asymptomatic for tuberculosis at baseline and started on first-line antiretroviral therapy. She deteriorated rapidly over the subsequent 10 days, presenting with night sweats, cough, and abdominal pain, fulfilling clinical criteria for urinary lipoarabinomannan testing.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recently diagnosed HIV infection, ART-naive until initiating first-line antiretroviral therapy 10 days prior. Prior medical history, travel, or TB exposures not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports night sweats, cough, and abdominal pain; denies hemoptysis, vomiting, or diarrhea. Home medications: first-line ART. Allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Assessed and met WHO clinical criteria for rapid diagnostic lipoarabinomannan testing; specific physical examination findings not documented.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis unmasked by immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (unmasking TB-IRIS) following first-line antiretroviral therapy initiation.
Confirmation: AlereLAM urine assay was strongly positive (4+); sputum and urine specimens were submitted for Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and mycobacterial culture.
Differentials ruled out: Acute antiretroviral adverse reaction and alternative opportunistic infections.
Treatment & Outcome: Promptly started on standard anti-tuberculosis therapy alongside continued antiretroviral therapy and supportive care.
